rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Six trends, one contest. Across a period Z_eff climbs (same-shell shielding is poor): **radii shrink** (Na 186 → Cl 99 pm), **ionisation energy climbs** with two dips — Be→B (2s² vs 2p¹) and N→O (half-filled vs pairing) — **electron affinity and electronegativity rise** (Cl most negative EA, F highest EN), and **metallic character falls**.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Z_eff = Z − σ (drives every trend) - M(g) → M⁺(g) + e⁻, IE₁; IE₁ < IE₂ < IE₃ - Isoelectronic radius ∝ 1/Z (approx) - Pauling EN: F 4.0 > O 3.5 > N 3.0 > Cl 3.0 … Cs 0.7

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **IE dips vs steady rise:** the period trend is "increases with two dips" — Be→B and N→O. A flat "increases" answer misses the marks reserved for the irregularities.  ·  **Cation shrinkage is not just electron loss:** losing the whole outer shell (Na⁺) dominates; but even same-shell loss (Fe³⁺ vs Fe²⁺) shrinks the ion because Z_eff per electron rises.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Atomic radius decreases across a period because the increasing effective nuclear charge pulls the same shell inward."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Na IE₁ = 496 → IE₂ = 4562 kJ mol⁻¹*** — a 9× jump: the second electron comes from the neon core. Successive-IE jumps are how shell structure was proven.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Verified PYQ: NEB 2022 3m — explain IE₁(Mg) > IE₁(Al) and r(Na) > r(Cl) (solved above). Other items are NEB-style practice.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — One Contest, Six Trends Atomic radius, ionic radius, ionisation energy, electron affinity, electronegativity and metallic character are not six facts to memorise — they are **six readings of one contest**: effective nuclear charge (Z_eff) pulling electrons in versus shells and shielding pushing them out.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Atomic radius - **Definition problem:** an electron cloud has no edge, so radius is defined operationally: - **Covalent radius:** half the internuclear distance between two bonded identical atoms (Cl–Cl → 99 pm). - **van der Waals radius:** half the closest distance between non-bonded atoms (larger than covalent).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Across: small, tight, greedy, non-metallic. Down: big, loose, generous, metallic." IE dips: "Be-B = s vs p; N-O = half-filled vs pair." Isoelectronic: more protons, smaller ion.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2022 (3m): Explain the periodic irregularities: (a) IE₁ of Mg is greater than that of Al although Mg is to the left of Al; (b) the atomic radius of Na is greater than that of Cl.** — **(a)** Mg = [Ne] 3s², Al = [Ne] 3s² 3p¹.…  ·  **NEB-style (3m): How do atomic radii vary across a period and down a group? Give one reason for each.** — **Across a period:** radius decreases (Li 152 → F 71 pm; Na 186 → Cl 99 pm) — electrons enter the same shell while Z_eff rises, pulling the shell inward.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: For irregularity questions, always write both configurations first (Mg 3s², Al 3s²3p¹) — the subshell contrast is the mark-earner; the numbers (738 vs 578) are garnish.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Irregularities are the exam:** Mg > Al (3s² filled vs 3p¹) and Na > Cl radius (Z_eff on the same shell) — NEB 2022's pair; add Be→B and N→O for the complete IE picture.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Radius: covalent/van der Waals/metallic definitions; decreases across (Z_eff ↑), increases down (new shell). Cation < atom < anion; isoelectronic size falls as Z rises. IE rises across (dips Be→B: 2s² vs 2p¹; N→O: half-filled vs pairing), falls down; IE₁ < IE₂ < IE₃ with a huge jump at core crossing.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Francium is often cited as the most metallic element, but Cs is the *practically* most reactive metal — Fr is so radioactive (half-life 22 minutes) that bulk chemistry is unobservable.

Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 NEB 2022 (3m, verified PYQ) — the two irregularities **(a) IE₁(Mg) > IE₁(Al) although Mg lies left of Al.** Mg: [Ne] 3s²; Al: [Ne] 3s² 3p¹. Mg's first electron comes from a **completely filled, stable 3s²** subshell; Al's comes from the higher-energy, shielded **3p** electron, which is easier to remove. Values: Mg 738 vs Al 578 kJ mol⁻¹.…  ·  **Periodic trends — across a period / down a group** | Property | Across a period | Down a group | Famous exception | |---|---|---|---| | Atomic radius | Decreases | Increases | noble-gas radii (van der Waals) larger | | Ionisation energy | Increases | Decreases | Be→B and N→O dips | | Electron affinity | Increases (overall) | Decreases | F < Cl | |…

rows.text: ## 5. Comparison Tables **IE vs EA vs EN** | Basis | Ionisation energy | Electron affinity | Electronegativity | |---|---|---|---| | Process | Losing an electron | Gaining an electron | Attracting shared pair in a bond | | Atom state | Isolated gaseous | Isolated gaseous | **Bonded** atom | | Quantity | Energy…  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **Radius dip exceptions:** noble-gas radii are **van der Waals** radii — larger than the neighbouring halogen's covalent radius; do not read them as a trend break in bonding radius.  ·  **IE dips are about subshell stability:** Be→B is s² vs p¹ (energy level); N→O is half-filled vs paired (repulsion). Two different causes — quote the right one for the right pair.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **EA vs EN:** EA is measurable energy for an **isolated** atom; EN is a relative tendency of a **bonded** atom. Cl has the most negative EA but **F** has the highest EN.  ·  ## 7. Exam Application **NEB-style (2m): Why is IE₂ of sodium enormously higher than IE₁?** — After IE₁, Na⁺ is [Ne] (1s²2s²2p⁶); IE₂ must remove an electron from the **filled inner shell** against a much higher Z_eff — 4562 vs 496 kJ mol⁻¹.
